question: Is the newly localized original-cue block15 attention reader concentrated in one native head or distributed across heads?

searched: temporal_auxiliary writer head/module/attn15 prior and followup files
prior_art_search.relation: Attn15 was selected prospectively by the complete-module atlas; no writer-specific head split exists at this layer.

frozen_design.population: the same 32 A1 and 32 A2 original rows
frozen_design.writer_and_capture: unchanged exact block8H1 cue-source writer and captured downstream response
frozen_design.arms: complete attn15 response plus each of heads 0 through 8 independently
frozen_design.concentration_bar: one identical head is largest in both families and retains >=0.60 of the complete attn15 mean response in both

predictions.pred_a_authority_capability_and_writer_r: module authority matches, all native sides are capable, writer and complete-attn15 effects reproduce within 0.03 writer units
predictions.pred_b_same_head_is_largest: the same head has the largest signed mean response in A1 and A2
predictions.pred_c_single_head_concentrates_attn15: that head retains >=0.60 of complete attn15 in both families and is donorward on >=0.75 of rows
predictions.pred_d_all_heads_reported: complete plus all nine singleton arms have 32 rows per family and finite effects

terminal_rules.invalid: authority, capability, recurrence, coverage, or price fails
terminal_rules.screen: same concentrated head passes and is opened for source/operation confirmation
terminal_rules.null: valid head atlas is distributed; use greedy joint head selection with no threshold rescue

interpretation_limits: Singleton head responses are a localization screen; concentration requires a later joint-complement check.
A distributed null leads directly to registered greedy head selection.
No DAS or rank fit is used.
